facts.statement: Jucha is an extinct genus of plesiosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Jucha is an extinct genus of plesiosaur found in the Hauterivian (Early Cretaceous) Klimovka Formation of Russia.

facts.statement: The type species Jucha squalea is considered one of the most basal and oldest known definitive elasmosaurs.
facts.quote: The type species, J. squalea, was one of the basalmost and oldest definitive elasmosaurs known to date.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in 2007 near the village of Slantsevy Rudnik in European Russia.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, UPM 2756/1-53, housed on display at the Undorov Pleontological Museum, was discovered in 2007 in a layer of the Klimovka Formation in the vicinity of the Slantsevy Rudnik village near Ulyanovsk, European Russia.

facts.statement: The genus and species Jucha squalea were formally described in 2020 by Fisher and colleagues.
facts.quote: The new genus and species Jucha squalea was described in 2020 by Fisher et al.

facts.statement: The genus name Jucha honors a figure from Turkic demonology known for having snake skin and the ability to remove her head.
facts.quote: The genus is named after Jucha, a girl in Turkic demonology who has snake skin, can turn into a dragon, has lived for a thousand years, and can take off her head.

facts.statement: The genus name references the fact that the holotype fossil lacks a skull.
facts.quote: This refers to the lack of a skull in the holotype.

facts.statement: The specific epithet squalea refers to the mineral crust of mainly pyrite that preserved the holotype.
facts.quote: The holotype was preserved in a mineral crust composed of mainly pyrite, hence the specific epithet squalea, a Latin word meaning "coated" or "rugose".

facts.statement: Fully grown individuals of Jucha reached a length of approximately 5 meters.
facts.quote: When fully grown, Jucha grew up to around 5 m long.

facts.statement: Jucha lived during the Hauterivian stage, between 132.6 and 125.77 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Hauterivian (132.6 to 125.77 million years ago)

rejected.quote: It consists of 17 cervical vertebrae, nine dorsal vertebrae and one isolated neural spine, four caudal vertebrae, and parts of the forelimbs and hindlimbs.
